# Gengchou v2.5.1

v2.5.1 is a fix release. Its centrepiece is that informational tray balloons
have never been displayed since v2.4.1: every notification Gengchou raised to
report something that already happened was accepted by Windows and then
silently dropped. Quota window reset reminders are the visible casualty. It
also closes a privacy gap found while reviewing that work: a provider whose
access you had revoked was still having its local credentials read by the
detection sweep. The executable, settings, cache, and update identities are
unchanged.

## Changes

- Stop reading the credentials of a provider whose access you revoked. Access
  is granted once for every provider but revoked one at a time, and the
  detection sweep ignored the per-provider switch: it read every provider's
  file, Credential Manager entry and running WSL distribution on every pass.
  Revoking already stopped the polling and the usage, so nothing was sent
  anywhere, but the local read itself should never have happened. The two
  sweep fixes further down are what make this reachable in practice - until
  now the sweep was not running at all. A provider you never turned off is
  still read, which is the only way a newly installed one can be noticed. This
  covers the periodic and startup sweeps, the manual re-detection, and the
  credential watch that samples for a refreshed token on every poll pass.
  Older settings cannot tell a revocation from "never asked", so an upgraded
  `allow=false` becomes **needs review** instead of being guessed: silent
  reads stay off until you choose **Allow access** or **Keep closed** under
  Provider access. That review also offers **Decide later**, and defaults to
  it: closing the dialog or pressing Enter leaves the provider pending instead
  of recording a decision you did not make. **Detect providers again** asks the same choice per pending
  provider and says it will read local credentials for ongoing monitoring. A
  provider added by an upgrade that is not pending or revoked can still be
  discovered automatically. Showing a provider under **Providers** no longer
  grants access. `gengchou.exe --claude-auth-diagnostics` remains a user-triggered
  exception that reads local Claude credentials only to print a redacted
  report.
- Report a credential that exists but cannot be used as **Authentication
  failed** for Codex, Antigravity and Grok, rather than **Not detected**. A
  malformed or unreadable `auth.json`, or a Credential Manager entry that
  cannot be parsed, was indistinguishable from never having signed in, which
  pointed you at installing a CLI you already had. Claude already classified
  these correctly. A WSL probe is deliberately not classified this way: it
  cannot tell a distribution that has no credential from one that failed to
  answer, so it still moves on quietly to the next source.
- Fix a hang that could freeze Gengchou on start with its window already
  drawn. Three places asked which window owns the poll timer while holding the
  state lock, and answering that question takes the same lock when the
  process-level helper window could not be created.
- Log a failure to arm the main poll timer instead of discarding it. Nothing
  re-arms that timer on its own, so the failure used to stop all monitoring
  until the next manual refresh, with nothing in the log to say why.
- Fix a profile whose only usable provider is Grok never polling at all. The
  check that decides whether to start a poll read only the first three
  providers, so a setup showing and authorising Grok alone was treated as
  having nothing to poll and skipped every pass. A fresh install that detects
  Grok and nothing else lands exactly there. Affected since v2.5.0, where Grok
  was introduced.
- Fix every informational tray balloon. Gengchou destroyed the balloon's image
  handle as soon as `Shell_NotifyIcon` returned. That is correct for a tray
  icon's own image, which the shell copies during the call, but Windows 10 and
  11 render a tray balloon as a toast *after* the call returns, so the handle
  was already gone and nothing was drawn - while the call still reported
  success. Affected since v2.4.1: **quota window reset reminders**, the
  notification for a newly detected provider, and the one for a finished
  Claude CLI update. Warnings that require action, such as a rejected
  credential, were never affected.
- Fix the periodic provider detection sweep, which had never run. Its timer was
  armed on the taskbar-embedded widget window, whose window procedure has no
  branch for it, so every `WM_TIMER` was discarded. Also affected since v2.4.1.
  A provider installed and signed into after Gengchou's first run was therefore
  never announced.
- Run one detection sweep at startup on an existing installation, instead of
  waiting a full 30-minute interval for the first one. An upgrade that adds a
  provider now tells you about it while you are still there to notice, and
  quitting sooner than the interval no longer defers it again. Each provider is
  still announced at most once, ever.
- Notify about a provider that is not currently shown. Such a provider has no
  tray icon by definition, and per-provider icon mode removes the application
  icon as well, so the balloon had nowhere to attach. It now falls through to
  whichever icon the tray actually has, and a delivery that fails outright is
  written to the diagnostic log rather than discarded.
- Show the application icon in the notification area when no provider has been
  granted credential access, instead of one arbitrarily chosen provider's mark.
  Your per-provider icon preference is not modified; the provider icons return
  as soon as any provider is authorised again.
- Say what is true when a provider has no credential access, instead of
  claiming you declined it. A provider that was simply never granted access now
  reads "Gengchou has no access to X", and both cases point at Provider access
  rather than the context menu at large.
- Stop the credential watch from asking for a refresh on every tick after you
  revoke or hide a provider. It compared its new, smaller set of sources
  against a snapshot of the old one and read the difference as a changed
  credential; because it then failed to record which set the snapshot came
  from, the next tick did the same thing again, and so on until a poll happened
  to correct it. It now records the set with the snapshot, so the watch asks
  once and then goes quiet.
- Show and start polling a provider immediately when you allow it from
  **Provider access -> Detect providers again**. Answering the review there
  granted access and saved it, but the sweep that followed had nothing new to
  report - the provider was already allowed by then - so nothing refreshed the
  taskbar widget, the tray, or the usage until the next scheduled poll. The
  same answer given directly under **Provider access** was always applied at
  once.
- Show the Gengchou icon in the title bar of the credential access dialog.
- Stop the taskbar widget's hover tooltip from reappearing next to the detail
  popup after a click opens it.
